articles.title: Add a zone
articles.summary: Press + Add Zone (top of the ZONES list).
articles.what: Add a zone: 3 steps, in the order you do them. You need a paint loaded first.
when: You want to: add a zone.
how: Press + Add Zone (top of the ZONES list).
Tell it which pixels: PICK COLOR FROM CAR (zone panel > WHICH PIXELS) (click a colour on the car), then raise Tolerance (zone panel > WHICH PIXELS) until the whole area is covered.
Pick a look in the base material picker (zone panel > BASE). The preview updates as you go.
tips: Or just tell the helper in plain words: "make the hood gloss black"

faq.q: What do I need before I start?
faq.a: You need a paint loaded first.

faq.q: Can I do this by typing instead?
faq.a: Or just tell the helper in plain words: "make the hood gloss black".

faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong

mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

articles.title: Get it into iRacing
articles.summary: Set iRacing Car Folder + iRacing User ID (top bar) (the User ID is your iRacing customer ID).
articles.what: Get it into iRacing: 3 steps, in the order you do them. You need a paint loaded first.
when: You want to: get it into iracing.
how: Set iRacing Car Folder + iRacing User ID (top bar) (the User ID is your iRacing customer ID).

In iRacing open the car’s paint shop / garage: the custom paint loads there.

faq.q: What do I need before I start?
faq.a: You need a paint loaded first.

faq.q: Is the User ID my car number?
faq.a: No. It is your iRacing Customer ID, 4 to 7 digits (helmet icon top right in iRacing, then Profile).

faq.q: Which folder should I pick as the car folder?
faq.a: The folder of the car you are driving: not a file, not the main paint folder, not a helmet or suit folder. Pick it from the car menu next to iRacing Car Folder.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: Your paint renders but never appears in iRacing
mistakes.cause: The User ID box holds a car number or another ID, and every file name carries it
mistakes.fix: Type your Customer ID (4 to 7 digits) and render again, then press Ctrl+R in iRacing.

mistakes.symptom: RENDER succeeds but iRacing finds no files
mistakes.cause: The car folder is not the folder of the car you drive
mistakes.fix: Open the car menu, pick your car and read the folder name.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Judge the car in the sim at driving distance after Ctrl+R, not only in the zoomed-in preview.

articles.title: Change only the shine (keep your colours)
articles.summary: In BASE COLOR dropdown (zone panel > BASE) choose "Use source paint (spec only)".
articles.what: Change only the shine (keep your colours): 3 steps, in the order you do them. You need a zone and a zone selected first.
when: You want to: change only the shine (keep your colours).
how: In BASE COLOR dropdown (zone panel > BASE) choose "Use source paint (spec only)".
Pick a FOUNDATION finish in the base material picker (zone panel > BASE) (f_chrome, f_metallic, f_pearl, Matte ...): it changes only metal / roughness / clearcoat.
The flat preview barely changes on spec-only work: check the channel previews under the LIVE PREVIEW (COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT).
aliases: change only the shine keep your colours

faq.q: What do I need before I start?
faq.a: You need a zone and a zone selected first.

faq.q: What do the spec channels mean?
faq.a: Red is metal, green is roughness (0 is a mirror), blue is clearcoat (16 is the glossiest, higher is duller) and alpha is the specular mask.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: The shine looks wrong
mistakes.cause: The shine was judged in the colour view, which cannot show it
mistakes.fix: Open the R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT views in the preview.

mistakes.symptom: Chrome looks dark or grey in the sim
mistakes.cause: iRacing multiplies the paint by the metal, so a dark paint under metal turns dark; flat mirror metal also reflects a cloudy sky
mistakes.fix: Use a near-white paint under chrome or a Foundation chrome finish with Source colours kept, and try a track with a brighter sky.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Look at the three spec views, not only the colour view; most surprises hide in the spec.

articles.title: Load a paint
articles.summary: Drag your paint file (a .tga or a layered .psd) onto the SOURCE area in the centre, or use Open in the top bar.
articles.what: Load a paint: 3 steps, in the order you do them.
when: You want to: load a paint.
how: Drag your paint file (a .tga or a layered .psd) onto the SOURCE area in the centre, or use Open in the top bar.
For a layered PSD use Open Layered in the LAYERS panel (right column): each layer becomes its own row.
When it shows in SOURCE, the LIVE PREVIEW fills in and it can read your car.

faq.q: Which files open with layers?
faq.a: PSD, XCF and ORA with the PSD/XCF/ORA button. Flat TGA, PNG and JPEG open without layers.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: Layers are missing after opening a PSD
mistakes.cause: Text, shape and adjustment layers are not plain pixels and cannot import
mistakes.fix: Rasterize them in your editor, save and open the file again.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Open the car template at its normal 2048 size; never resize the canvas first.

articles.title: Add a logo or picture
articles.summary: In the LAYERS panel (right column) press + Layer and pick the image file.
articles.what: Add a logo or picture: 2 steps, in the order you do them. You need a paint loaded first.
when: You want to: add a logo or picture.
how: In the LAYERS panel (right column) press + Layer and pick the image file.
Move / scale it with Move in the tool row (top: Move, Pick, Color, Wand, Lasso, Rect, Brush, Fill, Erase); finishes can then be limited to that layer.

faq.q: What do I need before I start?
faq.a: You need a paint loaded first.

faq.q: How do I keep numbers and sponsors untouched?
faq.a: Limit the zone to the body layer with Restrict to layer, or use a Foundation finish with Source colours, which changes only the shine.

faq.q: What scale looks fine on a whole car?
faq.a: Start around 0.5x. Scale (pattern) runs 0.10x to 4.0x and Base Scale 0.05x to 5.0x; 1.0x is normal and smaller is finer.

mistakes.symptom: Numbers or sponsors changed colour or finish
mistakes.cause: The zone covered every layer, not just the body
mistakes.fix: Set Restrict to layer to the body layer only, or add a layer restriction to the zone.

mistakes.symptom: A texture looks like boulders or a fishing net
mistakes.cause: The scale is too large for a whole-car sheet
mistakes.fix: Lower Scale (pattern) or Base Scale toward 0.5x and judge at 100 percent zoom.

protips: Select logos and numbers by layer name, not by colour: exact edges, no colour bleed.
Lower the scale first, then judge at 100 percent; it is the cheapest fix.

articles.title: Add a spec pattern (sparkle, flake, brushed)
articles.summary: Open SPEC PATTERNS (zone panel > SPEC PATTERNS) and add a layer (gold flake, pearl micro, brushed ...).
articles.what: Add a spec pattern (sparkle, flake, brushed): 3 steps, in the order you do them. You need a zone and a zone selected first.
when: You want to: add a spec pattern (sparkle, flake, brushed).
how: Open SPEC PATTERNS (zone panel > SPEC PATTERNS) and add a layer (gold flake, pearl micro, brushed ...).
Set Opacity and Scale; Channels M / R / C choose metal, roughness, clearcoat.
Spec patterns change the SHINE, not the colour: look at the channel previews under the LIVE PREVIEW (COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) or render to see them.

faq.a: You need a zone and a zone selected first.

faq.q: What scale looks fine on a whole car?
faq.a: Start around 0.5x. Scale (pattern) runs 0.10x to 4.0x and Base Scale 0.05x to 5.0x; 1.0x is normal and smaller is finer.

faq.q: What do the spec channels mean?
faq.a: Red is metal, green is roughness (0 is a mirror), blue is clearcoat (16 is the glossiest, higher is duller) and alpha is the specular mask.

faq.q: Does the preview change my iRacing files?
faq.a: No. The preview never writes into your iRacing folder; only RENDER does.

mistakes.symptom: A texture looks like boulders or a fishing net
mistakes.cause: The scale is too large for a whole-car sheet
mistakes.fix: Lower Scale (pattern) or Base Scale toward 0.5x and judge at 100 percent zoom.

mistakes.symptom: The shine looks wrong
mistakes.cause: The shine was judged in the colour view, which cannot show it
mistakes.fix: Open the R METAL, G ROUGH and B COAT views in the preview.

mistakes.symptom: The preview looks stale or wrong
mistakes.cause: It was not refreshed after a change
mistakes.fix: Press F5 over the preview, then diagnose.

protips: Lower the scale first, then judge at 100 percent; it is the cheapest fix.
Look at the three spec views, not only the colour view; most surprises hide in the spec.

faq.q: How do I keep numbers and sponsors untouched?
faq.a: Limit the zone to the body layer with Restrict to layer, or use a Foundation finish with Source colours, which changes only the shine.

mistakes.symptom: Numbers or sponsors changed colour or finish
mistakes.cause: The zone covered every layer, not just the body
mistakes.fix: Set Restrict to layer to the body layer only, or add a layer restriction to the zone.

protips: Select logos and numbers by layer name, not by colour: exact edges, no colour bleed.
